Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed head-on motor vehicle collision with complaints of right shoulder pain and restricted
range of motion. The reported mechanism of injury is consistent with the force of the collision and with the clinical presentation.
Examination revealed positive findings on several provocative tests, including pain with resisted abduction and a limited arc of
motion, while other tests, including neurovascular assessment and strength testing of the distal extremity, returned within normal
limits. No prior injury to the right shoulder is documented in the available history. The patient completed a course of 25 visits
consisting of manual therapy, therapeutic exercise, and home program instruction. Treatment duration was somewhat longer than
typically expected for this type of injury, reflecting a gradual but incomplete recovery in range of motion. Billing records
reviewed for this episode of care show no duplicate or repeated charges for the same services.
